name: Overcurrent or Heat Sink Overheated
meaning: Overcurrent flowed through the SERVOPACK's power transistors (IGBT), or its heat sink overheated.
symptoms: Alarm at servo ON or during acceleration; may not reset.
causes: Short or ground fault in the motor or cable; failed IGBT; heat sink overheating from a failed fan or blocked airflow; wrong motor connection.
checks: With power off, megger the motor and cable; check the U, V, W wiring; check the fan and airflow.
repairable: Yes: IGBT and power stage repair is common on SGDH units.
service: Servo drive repair; servo motor repair

name: Regeneration Error Detected
meaning: The SERVOPACK detected a fault in its regenerative (braking) circuit.
symptoms: Alarm at power-on or while braking.
causes: Regenerative resistor disconnected or burnt out; failed regenerative transistor; wrong resistor setting.
checks: Check the regenerative resistor and its jumper or wiring; measure its resistance with power off.
repairable: Yes: regenerative transistor faults are repairable.

name: Main Circuit Power Supply Wiring Error
Overvoltage
meaning: The main circuit DC voltage went too high.
symptoms: Alarm during deceleration or with a high supply voltage.
causes: Deceleration too fast for the load; regenerative resistor too small or failed; supply voltage too high.
checks: Note whether the alarm happens while braking; check the regenerative resistor; measure the supply voltage.
repairable: Often settings or resistor related; repairable when the voltage sensing has failed.

name: Undervoltage
meaning: The main circuit DC voltage dropped too low.
symptoms: Alarm during acceleration or on supply dips.
causes: Low or missing supply voltage; supply dips; failed rectifier or capacitors.
checks: Measure the main circuit supply voltage under load.
repairable: Yes, when the SERVOPACK's power circuit is the cause.

name: Overload: High Load
meaning: The motor ran well above its rated torque for several seconds (high-load overload).
symptoms: Alarm during heavy moves or at start.
causes: Mechanical binding or jam; brake not releasing; wrong wiring of the motor or encoder; motor fault.
checks: Check that the brake releases; check the mechanics for binding; check the motor and encoder wiring.
repairable: Often mechanical; motor or drive repair when wiring and mechanics check out.
service: Servo motor repair; servo drive repair

name: Overload of Surge Current Limit Resistor
Encoder Backup Error
meaning: All power to the absolute encoder was lost, so its stored position data was cleared.
symptoms: Alarm at power-on, often after a battery change or a disconnected cable.
causes: Backup battery dead or removed while power was off; encoder cable disconnected; failed encoder.
checks: Replace the backup battery with power on; set up the absolute encoder again; if it returns, check the encoder.
repairable: Usually a battery or setup issue; repairable when the encoder has failed.

name: Absolute Encoder Clear Error and Multiturn Limit Setting Error
Encoder Communications Error
meaning: The SERVOPACK cannot communicate with the motor's serial encoder.
symptoms: Alarm at power-on or intermittently while moving.
causes: Encoder cable damaged or disconnected; noise on the encoder cable; failed encoder; faulty encoder interface in the SERVOPACK.
checks: Inspect the encoder cable and connector; check shield grounding; try a known-good cable.
repairable: Yes: encoder replacement and SERVOPACK interface repair.
service: Encoder repair; servo motor repair; servo drive repair

name: Power Line Open Phase
meaning: One phase of the main power supply is missing.
symptoms: Alarm at power-on or under load.
causes: Blown fuse; loose terminal; contactor contact worn; failed input rectifier.
checks: Measure all three phases at the SERVOPACK input; check fuses and contactor.
repairable: Yes, when the SERVOPACK's input stage is the cause.

name: Not Completed within Set Time (application module)
